chunk_findings.detail: In the failed-merge outcome reason, `PD.dirt_hint(repo, cfg, r.err or r.out, repo)` passes `repo` as the worktree path to inspect for dirty files. For a merge into a worktree, `wt.path` is not `repo`, but the dirty files that caused the failure are in the worktree. The function has the same `borrowed`/`wt` information it already uses for `tree=None if borrowed else wt.path` above; passing `repo` again makes the dirty-file hint inspect the main repository instead of the actual worktree, so the user-facing failure reason loses or lies about the dirty files. Example: merge fails because `wt.path` has uncommitted files, while `repo` is clean; the returned reason will not point at the dirty worktree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_failed_landing_outcome

chunk_findings.detail: The only `callers` binding in this diff is a parameter of the inserted `_finish_merge`. The `_dispose_tree` call is an in-place edit of the existing `merge()` body (`callers=(called_from, shell_cwd)` → `callers=callers`), not a line moved into that helper. A landing that reaches dispose therefore raises `NameError: name 'callers' is not defined` and never removes or keeps the worktree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_dispose_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `_failed_landing_outcome` and `_finish_merge` are inserted ahead of the unchanged tail and nothing in the diff calls them. A failed git landing still never hits `GM.record_merge(..., "failed", ...)`, so `merge_failure_rate` still counts successes only, and `merge()` keeps the branches this extraction was supposed to remove. chunk_findings.detail: The failure reason is built with `PD.dirt_hint(repo, cfg, r.err or r.out, repo)`, passing `repo` as the tree path. The same helper already passes the correct merge tree path to `GM.record_merge` as `tree=None if borrowed else wt.path`. chunk_findings.detail: The only edit to `merge()` replaces the post-landing tail with module-level defs of `_failed_landing_outcome` and `_finish_merge` and never calls either helper. After a successful land, execution falls off the end of `merge()` where the old body used to spend the approval, record the gate, dispose the worktree and commit events; those statements now live only inside `_finish_merge`. A landed merge therefore returns `None` and leaves the approval, merge-gate event and worktree untouched. The failure helper is likewise dead, so a failed `git` land is no longer turned into the `worktree.merged` outcome this function builds.
